keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page dates Paletwa (January 2024), Minbya, Kyauktaw, Mrauk-U and Myebon (February), Buthidaung (18 May), Thandwe (17 July), Maungdaw (8 December) and Taungup (13 December) and says the AA gained 'most of Rakhine's territory'; Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, Ramree, Ponnagyun and Rathedaung see fighting but are not reported captured, and the page gives no township count or area. Only dated places are drawn, so the true hold is wider. Soft.

wars.outcome: By the end of 2024 the Arakan Army held Paletwa, Mrauk-U District, Buthidaung, Thandwe, Maungdaw and Taungup and 'most of Rakhine's territory'; Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, Ramree, Ponnagyun and Rathedaung were fought over; the Ann offensive began on 24 March 2024 and the AA took Taw Hein Taung base on 27 April 2024.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x for the post-2021 civil war (rule 5); Cliopatria ends its Burma shape without insurgent zones. Only the places the Arakan Army page dates are drawn; the page gives no township count ('14 of 17' is not on it), no area and no capture dates for Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, Ramree, Ponnagyun, Rathedaung, Ann or Gwa, so the 2024 shape understates the AA's hold. Pauktaw was taken and retaken in November 2023-January 2024 (two accounts on the AA page). The dossier ends in 2024 (Cliopatria's last year); the contest stays open. The page also reports the AA's administration ('Arakan People's Revolutionary Government'; CSIS: local governments by February 2025) and a vow of 10 April 2026 to capture all Rakhine by the end of 2027. No capital is named: Laiza is the former temporary headquarters, so the capital entry is a placeholder. The National Unity Government (16 April 2021) and the PDFs, the Kokang/MNDAA, TNLA and KIA gains of Operation 1027 (Laukkai, Lashio on 3 August 2024) are on the Myanmar civil war page without maps; no NUG dossier was written because no page maps its ground ('resistance groups achieved control of 40-50% of the country'; 'the Tatmadaw controlled under 40% of the country' by October 2023). Border band: union-of-myanmar and people-s-republic-of-bangladesh anchors (2000) cut to Chin State stand for Paletwa. Page budget: 6 pages including coordinate pages.
